chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Victrola and radio in the house
summary: Cranked Victrola, Philco radio and the morning and afternoon broadcasts of the Mills Brothers, Ink Spots, Eddie South and Wayne King.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Oh, we had records then. We had the Victrola at home!

Yeah, we had a Victrola, the kind that you have to crank up after every record, wind the record up and you have to change the needle after every five plays -- you know, change the needle. And later on, we got a little table model Philco radio, and we used to listen to the Mills Brothers every morning on the radio, and we used to listen to the Ink Spots. We used to hear every morning Eddie South, The Dark Angel of the Violin. This was a nationwide broadcast during those days, a live broadcast -- you could get these people every morning, you know.

Oh yeah. Those people, they came on in the morning. And then in the late afternoon we could get Guy Lombardo. We could get Frankie Trumbauer in the middle of the day. Are you familiar with Frankie Trumbauer, the C-melody saxophone player? We could get his band in the middle of the day. And then we could get Wayne King around about six o'clock. And in fact, his theme song was the first song I really learned how to play; "The Waltz You Sing For Me" was Wayne King's theme song. And he had a saxophone
section. All my people kept me with those sax...Guy Lombardo, all the saxophone players -- they'd have me listening to those saxophone bands, you know!
